snip.t: Respiratory signs – cough, hemoptysis, dyspnoea, sinusitis, otitis media: Pulmonary capillaritis (hemoptysis) is typical of ANCA vasculitis; chronic sinusitis points to granulomatosis with polyangiitis.
There is usually a viral cause, but disease may be\ncomplicated by lower respiratory tract infection, sinusitis, acute lar­\nyngitis or otitis media.

Abscesses in the frontal lobe are often caused by extension from sinusitis or orbital cellulitis, whereas abscesses located in the temporal lobe or cerebellum are frequently associated with otitis media and mastoiditis.
Complications: pneumonia, otitis media, diarrhoea, encephalitis, blindness and malnutrition.

snip.t: Give vitamin A to all children with measles, and watch for pneumonia, otitis media, diarrhoea and encephalitis.
Predisposing factors: Establish HIV status, ART history, prior tuberculosis or contact, sickle cell disease, recent otitis media, sinusitis, or base of skull trauma (rhinorrhoea/otorrhoea).
Nasal discharge and crusting, and otitis media also occur.
